why: A disabled input’s grey text: the painted colour is the fill, NOT `color`. Carrying `color` carried a lie — the contract minted #111111 for text the browser drew in #999999, with no receipt anywhere. MANIFEST EDIT (conformance-frontier round, R1): the engine's behaviour genuinely changed. `-webkit-text-fill-color` is now FOLDED INTO `color` at the read boundary (lib.ts foldTextFillColor, applied at both the capture and the replay/regate boundaries), so the case is re-declared CARRIED on the channel that carries it. Declaring it CARRIED on `color` is strictly STRONGER than the old UNSUPPORTED: it asserts the contract equals the PAINTED INK, so reverting the fold turns the case red (the reader would record color: rgb(17,17,17) and the prediction would fail) instead of passing on the mere presence of the string '-webkit-text-fill-color' in some receipt.

canvas.note: the text fill IS the ink the canvas draws — and now it is the ink the contract mints (verified in the subject browser: with the fill set, the rasterised glyph is rgb(153,153,153); the authored `color` rgb(17,17,17) paints nowhere)
